Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is a twin or triplet.
SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
HaveSiblingsSameAge(x, y) ::: x and y are siblings and are the same age.
ComplainsAboutSiblings(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x ∀y (HaveSiblingsSameAge(x, y)) → TwinOrTriplet(x) ∨ TwinOrTriplet(y) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainsAboutSiblings(x)) → ∃y (HaveSiblingsSameAge(x, y)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) → ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with family members.
∀x (SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x)) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
Conclusion:
(TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ DevelopsStrongBonds(luke)) ∨ (¬TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(luke)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.
